It may be used as a single drum (the capoeira tradition) or as a set of three (maculelê, candomblé, umbanda), assigned from high to low as lê, rum-pi and rum.

In maculelê and in the rites as many as three drums may be used at once, usually one for each pitch; in capoeira only one is traditionally used. It is a membranophone struck with the hands, and when listening, notice where the drum sits in the ritual and in the capoeira rhythms.

The atabaque is a tall wooden hand drum, a membranophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 211.221.1, found in Africa and Brazil. The body is traditionally Brazilian rosewood and the head calfskin; ropes wrap the body, linking a metal ring at the base to the head, and wooden wedges and a mallet adjust the tension, which is why it is called the rope-tuned atabaque. It is played by hand, comes in three sizes for low, middle and high, and is used in capoeira, maculelê and in Afro-Brazilian rites such as candomblé and umbanda, the last two of which regard it as a sacred instrument.
阿塔巴克鼓為膜鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs 編號 211.221.1: The atabaque is a membranophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 211.221.1. The body is traditionally made of Brazilian jacaranda wood and the head of calfskin; there is also a cowhide (couro de boi) component. The tuning system consists of ropes wrapped round the body, a metal ring near the base and wooden wedges pushed between the ring and the body; the source does not state the materials of other parts such as the hoop (aro) and the stand (suporte).
阿塔巴克鼓為膜鳴樂器，編號211.221.1，高身木製手鼓。非洲時期，繩栓調音型: The atabaque is a membranophone, 211.221.1, a tall wooden hand drum. In Africa the rope-and-peg tuned type had roughly the same distribution as the iron double bell agogo, running from the Niger along the Guinea coast west to Benin, Togo and Ghana; it later spread with the Ewe, Fon, Akan and Yoruba to Bahia, Suriname, Santo Domingo, Cuba and the southern United States. In Brazil it entered capoeira, maculelê and the candomblé and umbanda rites; the last two regard it as sacred and developed the three heights and ranges rum, rum-pi and lê. Rites use up to three drums, while capoeira traditionally uses only one.
阿塔巴克鼓音色深沉溫潤，具有濃厚的非洲鼓樂特色。其音域寬廣，可通過敲擊鼓面的不同: The atabaque has a deep, warm timbre with a strong African drumming character. Its range is wide, and striking the head in different places produces sounds from a deep accent to a clear high note. The drum has a warm low-mid resonance and carries well. Beside the bright, sharp conga the atabaque sounds fuller and more contained; beside the drum kit it has more of a raw, natural feel. The rope tuning lets the player control the pitch precisely, so the instrument can carry a wide range of expression. When several atabaques play together the sound is clearly layered with a long ring, which suits the rhythms of Brazilian samba and capoeira especially well.
